Could: give the 80 a name, e.g. a private `keyboardBarClearance` constant next to the comment. Then the next form with a Done bar can reuse the value instead of guessing it again.

<!-- prwatch -->

Done in e6602bc. The value is now `Theme.Spacing.keyboardBarClearance` (80), documented as the bottom content margin a scrolling form with text fields needs so its last field clears the keyboard's floating Done bar, which isn't part of the keyboard inset. `NutrientFormView` uses it. The value hasn't changed, and the build succeeds.

Could: this scrolls on every focus change, even when no on-screen keyboard appears (iPad with a hardware keyboard, or moving between fields while the keyboard is already up). Waiting for `keyboardDidShowNotification` (or checking the keyboard frame) would scroll only when something is covered. Fine to leave as is, since the scroll is harmless.

<!-- prwatch -->

Leaving it as is, as you suggest. When no on-screen keyboard appears, or it's already up, the scroll only nudges the field toward the upper third of what's visible: harmless, and it keeps the code free of keyboard-frame bookkeeping. If an iPad layout or a hardware-keyboard complaint comes up, the `keyboardWillShowNotification` frame is the place to gate it.
